artists.biography: Norman Quentin Cook, known professionally as Fatboy Slim, is an English musician and DJ who helped popularise the big beat genre in the 1990s. His music makes extensive use of samples from eclectic genres, combined with pop structures, processed rhythms and "sloganistic" vocals.
artists.name: Fatboy Slim

Fatboy Slim.biography: Norman Quentin Cook, known professionally as Fatboy Slim, is an English musician and DJ who helped popularise the big beat genre in the 1990s. His music makes extensive use of samples from eclectic genres, combined with pop structures, processed rhythms and "sloganistic" vocals.

perplexity.description:
Better Living Through Chemistry is Fatboy Slim's debut album, released on September 23, 1996, through Skint Records in the United Kingdom and Astralwerks in the United States. The album marked Norman Cook's emergence as a solo artist under the Fatboy Slim moniker and established him as a significant figure in the big beat movement that was gaining momentum throughout the mid-1990s. With a runtime of approximately 70 minutes, the album blends big beat, club/dance, funky breaks, trip-hop, and electronica into a cohesive electronic statement.

The album's title references DuPont's famous advertising slogan, reflecting the optimistic, sample-heavy aesthetic that defined much of 1990s dance music. Cook's production approach on Better Living Through Chemistry combined breakbeats, funk samples, and electronic textures into accessible yet sophisticated dance tracks. The album represented a turning point for electronic music in the mainstream, helping to popularize big beat beyond underground club culture.

Better Living Through Chemistry achieved significant commercial and critical success, becoming Fatboy Slim's first charting work and establishing the foundation for his subsequent prominence in electronic music. The album's success positioned Cook as one of the leading producers of the era and helped define the sound of late-1990s dance music, making it a landmark release in both his career and the broader history of electronic music.
